points.quote: Left, one key K that must somehow reach Bob; right, Bob's key pair
points.problem: The caption describes the two panels as left and right, but the figure stacks them: symmetric on top, asymmetric below, at both 375 px and 1440 px. 'Below, TLS uses...' then also reads as a third thing beneath, so the reader cannot map the caption onto the picture.
points.hint: Say 'Top' and 'middle' (or 'First/second'), or name the panels instead of left/right.

points.quote: stretching the attack from seconds of flooding to hours
points.problem: The revised paragraph says the port-randomisation patch stretched the attack to hours (a patched resolver poisoned in under ten hours). The Fig 11.7 caption (ch11-dns-p8) on the same page says the fix pushed the practical attack from minutes to years, and that Kaminsky made it practical 'in minutes'. A reader sees two incompatible figures for the same fact.
points.hint: Make the caption agree with the paragraph's seconds-to-hours account, or drop the competing numbers from one of them.

points.quote: each carry a keyed hash of the entire transcript
points.problem: 'Keyed hash' and 'transcript' are not introduced; Section 04 taught only plain hashing (no key). The reader is not told why a mismatch exposes tampering (each side hashes what it saw and compares), so the mechanism is a bare claim.
points.hint: One clause: each side hashes every handshake message it saw, mixed with the new key, and the two results must match.

points.quote: browsers send it as the CORS preflight
points.problem: The 'How it works' strip uses 'CORS preflight' (and 'JSON Merge Patch' / 'JSON Patch') with no earlier explanation in the book, so a newcomer has to look them up for a side note.
points.hint: Drop the CORS and JSON Patch asides, or reduce them to a plain-words clause.

points.problem: 'Walled-garden' is never defined and the three services are unexplained to a reader who does not know them, so the closing 'which is why' conclusion is hard to follow.
points.hint: Define in a phrase: closed online services that kept their members inside their own network.
